primitives.name: Real-Time Market Sensitivity Sampling
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method and system of the present invention utilize limited sampling to determine real-time market sensitivity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ΔP_opt:': 'Optimal price change (USD)', 'ΔS:': 'Market sensitivity sample size (dimensionless)', 'ΔC:': 'Computational budget allocation (dimensionless)', 'ΔT:': 'Time horizon window (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent samples drawn from heterogeneous demand distributions; bounded computational resources; stationary market microstructure within ΔT.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $\Delta S \rightarrow 0$, sample variance diverges; when $\Delta T$ exceeds market memory length, stationarity assumption fails.

primitives.name: Customized Dynamic Pricing with Promotions
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method and system of the present invention allow for customized dynamic pricing with promotions, discounts and bundling The method and system of the present invention enables a company using the system to offer different promotions to different customers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_i(t):': 'Price of item i at time t (USD)', 'C_i(t):': 'Base cost of item i (USD)', 'α_ij:': 'Promotional discount coefficient for bundle j applied to item i (dimensionless)', 'D_ij(t):': 'Binary indicator function for bundle j activation at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Additive separability of promotional effects across items; instantaneous promotion fulfillment; no cannibalization between bundles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $\sum_j \alpha_{ij} > 1$, resulting price becomes negative, invalidating the non-negativity constraint.

layer2.telemetry: Incremental revenue lift from promoted bundles relative to baseline pricing

primitives.name: Market Segmentation Based Optimal Price Setting
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method and system of the present invention may be used to segment the market, and managers using the system of the present invention may be informed of an optimal price for each market segment.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P*_k:': 'Optimal price for market segment k (USD)', 'R:': 'Revenue function (USD)', 'S_k:': 'State vector representing characteristics of segment k (dimensionless)', 'E:': 'Expectation operator over demand distribution given S_k'}
primitives.assumptions: Homogeneous behavior within segments; independent segment choices; stable segment membership over the planning horizon.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When segment variance exceeds population heterogeneity, optimal price becomes unstable; when new entrants disrupt segment composition, the solution reverts to uniform pricing.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Segmented Pricing & Customer Lifetime Value
layer2.telemetry: Price discrimination efficiency measured by the ratio of segmented vs. uniform profit margins
